transcript: When the little girl was placed in front of the raging bull, she instantly became a source of inspiration to young girls and like-minded men and women around the world. They often go to to the fearless girl to make their statements. She's become sort of a symbol of standing up to obstacles. It did not require people to put another type of person on a board because people were coming to my office. I also serve on the financial services committee and ranking on the capital markets committee. And particularly pension fund managers and fund managers, they wanted to know how many women on boards. I was able to pass roughly 24 bills out of the financial services committee this year, but I couldn't move the little girl. I couldn't move disclosure of how many women are wearing boards, and Chairman Hensseline said it was too radical. I don't see how it's radical to disclose information, and my bill was basically disclosing information so that investors and pension managers and others who were asking for this information. Incidentally, there have been a number of studies by financial institutions that have shown that when you have a gender-balanced board, it actually performs better. So many people are interested in that economic aspect of it. But I don't give up. That's why I'm ringing the bell every year for women's empowerment. And part of that empowerment is being able to move more women on boards. And I think if you disclose that information and people see that with women on the boards, they are actually even performing better than that would open up more opportunities for men.

So it's very unfair. So one way to justify that is to finally pass the Equal Rights Amendment, which would mean that then equality of rights could be enforced. Title VII, equality of treatment and employment, Title IX, equality of treatment and education, in sports, these are areas that they constantly try to chip away with. whether it protections that you would not be able to chip away with it. And I, for one, am tired of spending time trying to hold on to what we already have. I'd like to spend my time in working to make the country better and fair. If we ever help a country with their Constitution, as we did with Japan, as we did with Afghanistan and with other countries, then we make sure that it's in the Constitution.
